author: haiku
label: climb-06-01
changes: A2: added what KMS is and that the pod identity mechanism is not decided (open question 10).
A5: stated that the security on-call makes the read-only provider call and that the endpoint is not named (open question 12).
A7: old pods keep the keys from their own image; rolled-back pods read the old keys from their image, not the store, so the rollback path is explicit.
A8: added how the version-id check is done (manual query of the central log service, recorded in the migration record).
B1: added a step that logs secret names and version ids at startup, which A8 requires; noted that where APP_ENV is set is open (open question 11).
B4: stated that nothing triggers a refresh before the 5-minute timer and how in-flight calls keep their snapshot.
B5: stated the prefix list and that the filter catches only known prefixes.
Open questions: added 10 (pod identity mechanism), 11 (APP_ENV and store identity), 12 (read-only provider endpoint).
Rewrote the whole document into the skill's layout: summary paragraph, terms, runtime steps, rollout steps, local development and CI guard, failure table, open questions.
Split the document into separate sections for how the app runs (Part 1), how the migration rolls out (Part 2) and local development and CI (Part 3), so the two are not mixed.
Added a terms list that defines every term a newcomer would need, including KMS, live and sandbox keys, pod, image, readiness, liveness, ReplicaSet, holder and bake period.
Replaced cross-references such as A7, B4 and open question 10 with the section and step names, so each step can be read on its own. Open questions are numbered only at the end.
Q8: stated that the image decides which code path runs, and that there is no switch in config. Added what happens if the new code cannot find its keys.

Q9: stated that the cluster halts only for pods that are not ready, that the on-call pauses by hand for provider rejections, and that rollback is redeploying the previous image. Added an open question for the rollback tool and who runs it.
Q10: stated that the plan sets no time limit on a crash loop. Added an open question on whether to page after a set time.
Q11: added the on-call's steps for a bad stored version: pause, roll back, write a corrected version, and let the refresh or a restart pick it up.
Q12: stated which pods read the store and when, and that old pods read only their own config. Flagged the unknown about whether a write is the current value at once as an open question.
Q13: defined the fallback during the bake as a rollback to a pre-migration image, and said it works only until the revocation gate.
Q14: stated that /healthz keeps its path for readiness but changes meaning. Added a separate liveness path and said the service owner changes the probe config in the same PR.
Added a failure table (Part 4) that summarizes each failure, its effect and who acts. The step-level failure notes are kept.

Kept every stated fact from the brief and the first version, including the 4 replicas, identity, maxUnavailable: 0, the 30-day log retention, the 5-minute refresh, the retry policy, the known key prefixes, core dumps, fake test values, the staging and dev secrets, and the make run-offline mode.
Moved the CI guard into its own section and kept the same-PR rule (added with the yaml change, not earlier).
Kept the rotation cadence as an open question and did not pick a cadence.

Summary rewritten: it now says how the current system works (keys in config/app.yaml, read once, copied into every image) before the main flow, and why the order is shaped as it is (old pods keep their own keys, so rollback works until revocation). Answers the newcomer's question about the overall shape.

Terms section added and expanded: defined secret store, KMS, live vs sandbox key, provider, identity, version id, pod, image, pre-migration image, old ReplicaSet, readiness, liveness, rollout, maxUnavailable, rollback, holder, refresh, bake period, revoke, admission rule, stub client, and central log service. Each is defined in one plain line.

Split into two sections: how the app reads keys at runtime, and how the migration rolls out. Local development and the CI guard are a third section. Runtime steps were un-numbered so they cannot be confused with the rollout steps.
Added that the image alone decides the code path, with no config switch (answers the question on how a new pod knows to read the store).

Added that old and new pods serve at once and why that is safe: each key in use is valid at its provider, and each new key is checked before any pod uses it (answers the question on mixed-version serving).

Startup loading now logs each secret name and version id, which the rollout check reads (answers how the version-id check is done). Stated that the check is manual via the central log service unless automated.
Requests in flight keep their snapshot, and no refresh happens sooner than 5 minutes or on demand (answers the in-flight refresh question).
Logging filter described as a backstop only that catches the three known prefixes and nothing else. Read-only provider check described as made by security on-call, with the endpoint left open.
Stated that old pods never read the store, and that prod pods do not read it before step 7. The question of whether a new write becomes visible to every read at once is listed as an open question.

Stated that the cluster halts a rollout only for pods that never become ready. A ready pod rejected by a provider is paused by hand. Rollback is redeploying the previous image tag, run by on-call or the service owner. The tool is open.

Recovery from a bad store value is written as an ordered sequence: pause, roll back, write a corrected version, then resume. The recovery is the manual path because the app does not detect bad values.
Bake-period fallback explained: it means rolling back to a pre-migration image, which works only until the admission rule blocks those images.
Probe design clarified: readiness stays on /healthz, liveness needs its own path, and a pod with no keys must not fail liveness. Old pods keep the old meaning.
Crash-loop behaviour stated plainly: no time limit is set, and only a store fix or a rollback stops the loop. Paging after a set time is an open question.
Cross-references by codes such as R3 or Q7 removed; cross-references now name the step or topic. The failure table is kept as a quick reference, and each step still has its own If it fails line.

Cut: no requirement, limit, number, setting or rule was removed. The duplicated failure text in the first version's Part 4 is kept only as the summary table, since every row also appears in a step. Retry, timeout and cadence values are unchanged.

Open questions kept in full: all 14, including rotation cadence (not decided), two live keys per provider, bake period, retry count, staging, store version semantics, fallback on rejected values, old keys in logs, probe paths, pod identity, APP_ENV and store identity, read-only endpoint, rollback tool, and crash-loop time limit. Question 6 now also covers whether a new write is visible to every read at once.
No new mechanism (lock, lease, retry queue or takeover rule) was added. The length is about the same as the first version, well within 1.5 times it.
holes: Q1: What is the "managed secret store" and "KMS" here, and how does a pod prove who it is to the store (what makes it "identity orders-api-prod")? (author: The brief names 'the managed secret store' and a per-environment KMS key but not the products. KMS is the key management service that encrypts the stored values at rest. The brief names the identity orders-api-prod but not how a pod proves it holds that identity. The mechanism is not decided and is open question 10. A2 now says so.)

Q3: How does the new code know which environment it is in and which store to talk to? Where does APP_ENV get set in prod, and how does the pod get its store identity? (author: The brief does not say where APP_ENV is set in prod or how a pod gets the identity it uses to read the store. Only the requirement that the environment name is non-secret is stated. This is open question 11.)
